pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
We are delighted to welcome you to Everest Community Academy. Our school is an integral part of our local community and together we will ensure Everest is a school we are all proud of. Our core values - aspire, enrich, belong - guide everything we do, every day. We are unashamedly focused on achieving the best educational outcomes for our students. We are determined to be the school of choice for parents and students in the local area, and to be recognised as a school that values each member of our community.
At Everest, our overarching intent is to open doors for all our students as we unapologetically pursue the best outcomes for all our students. We achieve this through a broad and balanced curriculum that sparks curiosity, elevates aspirations, and nurtures a lifelong love for learning. Our commitment extends beyond academic excellence; we aim to empower students socially and emotionally as well.
We prepare our students for the future by equipping them with essential skills. Whether they choose higher education, vocational training, or employment, we ensure they have a clear path ahead.
Enrichment goes beyond academics. It encompasses experiences, skills, and personal development. At Everest, we believe in providing opportunities that enrich students’ lives—whether through extracurricular activities, cultural exposure, or character-building opportunities.
Belonging matters. Our curriculum promotes inclusivity and celebrates diversity in all its forms. Across subject areas, we help students appreciate different perspectives and build compassion for others. Our school community values each voice, providing a safe space for expression.
We welcome visits from students and parents and would encourage you to contact the school office by email to info@Everestcommunityacademy.org, or by telephone on 01256 961330 to arrange a visit. Our staff and students will be happy to show you around and answer any questions you may have about our school. We hope this has given you a sense of Everest Community Academy and the immense pride we have in our school. By working in partnership with all members of our community, we strive to inspire, enrich, and provide a nurturing environment where every student thrives.
Alison Reid | Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
At Everest, we are unashamedly focused on achieving the best educational outcomes for our students. We are determined to be the school of choice for parents and students in the local area, and to be recognised as a school that values each member of our community.
Ensuring our students leave Everest with good outcomes and well-prepared for the future is at the heart of all we do. Every child at Everest deserves the opportunity to succeed and thrive in all aspects of their lives; they are valued members of our school and the wider community. As we work together, my goal is to prepare your children for the wealth of opportunities awaiting them beyond our doors.
We believe our learners thrive in an environment which is stable and consistent and so we work hard to ensure we have clear routines and expectations. Our dedicated and highly skilled staff are committed to ensuring their learning is challenging, relevant and enjoyable. We want your children to enjoy their time here, feel safe, and form enduring friendships. Above all, we wish to provide a curriculum that creates a firm foundation of the knowledge and skills for life.
Everything we do is driven by our core values: aspire, enrich, belong.
Aspire: This value encourages students to set ambitious goals and dream big. It’s about having a vision for their future and working diligently to achieve it. Success is an attitude! Aspiration drives growth and motivates students to reach their full potential.
Enrich: Enrichment goes beyond academics. It encompasses experiences, skills, and personal development. At Everest, we believe in providing opportunities that enrich students’ lives—whether through extracurricular activities, cultural exposure, or character-building opportunities.
Belong: Feeling a sense of belonging is crucial. Our school community fosters inclusivity, celebrates diversity, and ensures that every student feels valued. When students belong, they thrive academically and emotionally.
Over the year ahead, to achieve the best outcomes for all our students, we will focus on three main priorities:
High Expectations: We will hold every member of our community to high standards of conduct and engagement. Our aspirations for all students will be unwavering.
Engaging Curriculum: Our curriculum will be challenging, relevant, and broad. It will ignite curiosity and actively engages our students in their learning journey.
Quality Teaching: Every student deserves high-quality, adaptive teaching in every lesson, every day. A love of reading will be fostered, and we will work hard to design and deliver lessons which ensure all students thrive.
To ensure our leaders are accountability for the improvement of the school a strategic plan is produced annually.
The document is ratified by the local governing committee and regularly reviewed during the school year.
Promotion of British Values
At Everest Community Academy we recognise not only the importance of allowing students to flourish academically but we also embrace our wider role in preparing them for their adult life beyond the formal examined curriculum. Part of our role in that preparation is ensuring that we promote and reinforce British values to our students.
The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy and considered them to be democracy, rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs. At Everest Community Academy these values are reinforced in a pervasive manner and permeate the school community.
The examples that follow are an indication of some of the many ways we seek to embed British values at Everest Community Academy and should be seen as an indication of our approach rather than an exhaustive list.
Democracy
At Everest Community Academy the principle of democracy is consistently reinforced, with the democratic process being employed for important decisions within the school community, for instance, elections held for our Head Boy and Girl and prefects. The principle of democracy is explored in History and Religious Studies, as well as in form time, discrete PSHE days and assemblies.
The rule of law
The importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, is consistently reinforced throughout regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school assemblies. Students are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police are regular parts of our calendar and help reinforce this message.
Individual liberty
Within Everest Community Academy, students are actively encouraged to make independent choices, knowing that they are in a safe, secure and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for students to make choices safely, through the provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Students are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and receive advice about how to exercise these safely, for example through our exploration of E-Safety in Computing and form time activities.
Mutual respect
Respect is at the core of our school ethos and is modelled by students and staff alike. The school promotes respect for others and this is reiterated through our classroom and learning environments. In line with our commitment to democracy students at Everest Community Academy are always able to voice their opinions and we foster an environment where students feel safe to disagree with each other. Mutual respect is embraced throughout the curriculum from the concept of fair play in PE to a number of buddy programmes which promote mutual respect between students across different year groups within the school.
Tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs
This is achieved through equipping students with the ability to understand their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity within the school community. Students are actively encouraged to share their faith and beliefs within the school. Our Religious Education curriculum provides a broad and balanced education on a range of faiths, religions and cultures.
Should you feel that the school is not meeting this requirement, you should contact the school office and request to express your concerns with the Headteacher. Likewise, if you feel that anyone working at the school is undermining these values you should report this to the Headteacher.

English
Our English curriculum at Everest is designed around the concept of DARE. We want our students to be daring academics, and to provide every student with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to achieve.
Diverse – exposing students to a wide range of voices, perspectives and literary traditions.
Aspirational – challenging students with ambitious texts, ideas and opportunities.
Resilient – encouraging perseverance, reflection and independence in learning.
Engaging – capturing imaginations and creating passionate learners.
Across the English department, students are challenged to produce high-quality work and are inspired by writers from other places, times and worlds. Beyond the classroom, they enjoy opportunities to perform, experience theatre and poetry, and participate in extracurricular activities that enrich their understanding of literature and language.
Through the study of fiction, non-fiction, poetry and drama, students develop the disciplinary knowledge and skills of English: describing, exploring, interpreting, analysing and evaluating texts, drawing inferences, summarising ideas accurately, and communicating with precision. They learn to read critically, analyse writers' methods, understand how language shapes meaning and craft their own writing for a range of audiences and purposes.
Curriculum Statement
Students engage with significant human experiences and enduring themes including loss and guilt, power and conflict, identity, relationships, community, perspective, and individual and shared experiences. Through these studies, they become intellectually curious, develop informed opinions, evaluate differing viewpoints, recognise bias and challenge interpretations. Performance, debate, presentation and discussion enable students to develop confident and articulate voices.
As our students progress through the curriculum, they encounter increasingly challenging texts and concepts, building confidence and independence. They develop a rich and ambitious vocabulary, secure knowledge of grammar and language structures, and increasingly sophisticated analytical and writing skills across a range of genres and contexts.

Mathematics
The mathematics department aims to empower students with confidence in their mathematical abilities. We believe that mathematical skills extend beyond the classroom. By fostering a deep understanding of mathematical principles, we equip our students to apply these skills effectively in various contexts.
In our lessons, students are challenged to reach their full potential. We encourage them to set high aspirations for themselves. Through rigorous teaching, we ensure that students not only grasp mathematical concepts but also understand the “why” behind techniques. This understanding allows them to make connections between different mathematical ideas.
We believe in nurturing creativity and critical thinking. Students have access to enrichment activities that encourage them to think outside of the box. This includes our weekly Maths Puzzle and participation in UKMT competitions. Our focus on problem solving, using logical and systematic approaches and real world maths helps to equip our students for their future.
We aim to create a safe and inclusive space where students feel comfortable sharing their ideas and exploring mathematical concepts. Collaboration is encouraged, allowing students to learn from one another and appreciate diverse perspectives. By fostering a sense of belonging, we empower students to express themselves confidently in mathematical language.

Art and Design
The Art curriculum aims to equip students with the knowledge, confidence, and skills to be creative learners and apply their skills to the wider world. It is designed to be aspirational for all students, with differentiation through teacher examples and past student work. The curriculum explores diverse artists, movements, and cultures to broaden students’ experiences and understanding of the world.
The curriculum emphasises skill development, with a clear progression from basic techniques to more advanced practices, building students’ confidence and readiness for GCSE. Regular feedback, including oral and FAR feedback, ensures that any gaps in understanding are addressed, and teaching is adapted to meet individual needs.
The classroom environment is calm and creative, encouraging independent learning, experimentation, and personal growth. Through relevant and engaging projects, students have opportunities to explore new materials and techniques while developing their artistic skills. Regular curriculum reviews ensure lessons remain relevant and engaging for all students.

pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
The vision of the MFL department is to develop students into competent, confident linguists with functional communication skills in the target language.
To achieve this vision, students will:
Overall students will be proud of their achievements and therefore have the confidence to demonstrate this regularly in lessons through helping each other and using the target language as much as possible in (and out) of lessons.
Opportunities for enrichment will be provided through the Language Leader’s Course offering students the opportunity to teach their chosen language to primary aged children. Trips to visit countries where the target language is spoken should be arranged on minimum of a bi-annual basis. Opportunities will be sought to invite Spanish speakers into school to work with MFL students, whenever possible. The European Day of Languages will be promoted across the school every 26th September.
Students will be enthused to develop a passion for the target language through engaging and relevant lessons where students understand why the content applies to them using real world contexts. Every other lesson will include a careers based question encouraging students to reflect on the importance of language learning and potential career opportunities linked to this subject.

Design Technology
Within our curriculum we strive to give students the knowledge, confidence and skills to be creative learners, as well as the confidence to apply these skills within the wider world. The 5 mains skills are research, design, make, evaluate and technical knowledge.
The sequence of our SOWs build on skills each topic, so students are practising and perfecting their skills within each project. This builds up their confidence in skills and work in order to do well in GCSE. We have interesting projects and SOW relating to things around us, we do lots of practical work and teacher demonstrations to engage the students. Building on skills within Technology is the main drive, along with giving students the opportunities to study relevant topics within the world we live in. Student enjoyment within a project is important, so students are engaged and learning. The atmosphere within Technology is mostly calm and creative, where students become independent learners who are engaged and enjoying their work. They have opportunities to use materials and tools not always available to them and enjoy seeing their work evolve.

Citizenship
The Humanities curriculum aims to cultivate curious, empathetic and critically engaged learners who understand their place in a complex, interconnected world. Through the disciplines of Citizenship, Geography, History and Religious Studies, we seek to empower students with the knowledge, skills and values needed to navigate society with confidence and integrity.
Students are equipped with the knowledge and skills to:
Understand the past, engage with the present, and prepare for the future
Appreciate diverse perspectives, cultures and beliefs
Respond to global, moral and political challenges with empathy and confidence
Through Humanities, students explore the world intellectually, ethically and socially, developing the ability to think deeply, speak purposefully, and act responsibly.
Citizenship Studies has the power to motivate and enable young people to become thoughtful, active citizens. Students gain a deeper knowledge of democracy, government and law, and develop skills to create sustained and reasoned arguments, present various viewpoints and plan practical citizenship actions to benefit society. They will also gain the ability to recognise bias, critically evaluate argument, weigh evidence and look for alternative interpretations and sources of evidence, all of which are essential skills valued by higher education and employers.

History
The Humanities curriculum aims to cultivate curious, empathetic and critically engaged learners who understand their place in a complex, interconnected world. Through the disciplines of Citizenship, Geography, History and Religious Studies, we seek to empower students with the knowledge, skills and values needed to navigate society with confidence and integrity.
Students are equipped with the knowledge and skills to:
Understand the past, engage with the present, and prepare for the future
Appreciate diverse perspectives, cultures and beliefs
Respond to global, moral and political challenges with empathy and confidence
Through Humanities, students explore the world intellectually, ethically and socially, developing the ability to think deeply, speak purposefully, and act responsibly.
History has the power to inspire and enable young people to understand the world around them by exploring the people, events and ideas that have shaped societies over time. Students gain a deeper knowledge of the past, developing an understanding of how and why change has occurred and the impact it has had on different individuals and communities. They learn to analyse and evaluate historical evidence, consider different interpretations and explore the significance of historical sources. History also develops critical thinking, research and communication skills, enabling students to question sources, recognise bias and draw well-supported conclusions. These transferable skills are highly valued by higher education institutions and employers alike.

Geography
The Humanities curriculum aims to cultivate curious, empathetic and critically engaged learners who understand their place in a complex, interconnected world. Through the disciplines of Citizenship, Geography, History and Religious Studies, we seek to empower students with the knowledge, skills and values needed to navigate society with confidence and integrity.
Students are equipped with the knowledge and skills to:
Understand the past, engage with the present, and prepare for the future
Appreciate diverse perspectives, cultures and beliefs
Respond to global, moral and political challenges with empathy and confidence
Through Humanities, students explore the world intellectually, ethically and socially, developing the ability to think deeply, speak purposefully, and act responsibly.
Geography has the power to inspire and equip young people with the knowledge and understanding to make sense of an ever-changing world. Students develop a deeper understanding of both human and physical processes, exploring the relationships between people, places and environments at local, national and global scales. They build skills in analysing data, interpreting maps, evaluating evidence and drawing well-reasoned conclusions about complex geographical issues. Geography also encourages students to think critically about challenges such as climate change, urbanisation and resource management, while developing the fieldwork enquiry, research and decision-making skills that are highly valued in higher education and the workplace.

pageCache.pageTitle: Food Technology and Catering - Subjects - Everest Community Academy
pageCache.text:
Food Technology and Catering
Promoting lifelong engagement in sport and a passion for health and exercise as well as independent skills and the knowledge to implement a healthy lifestyle.
The curriculum focus is primarily to develop practical skills to promote independence and provide the knowledge to allow students to eat a healthy balanced diet. SMSC plays a pivotal role in topic choice and the importance of developing life skills which will help students be self-sufficient and safe regarding cooking, health and hygiene outside of school. Key stage three is focused around preparing students with the skills to be independent with cooking and the knowledge of healthy eating and how this impacts their lives. This also facilitates student conversations and learning around how a healthy diet improves all aspects of health and exploring what a healthy and balanced diet looks like beyond just food. Teamwork plays a large part of developing students’ learning and resilience in practical and theory food lessons. Business projects and specific food projects are a focus at key stage three and students work in pairs in when taking part in practical lessons.
At GCSE, students are required to create their own menus and explore how this would be received in real life. The curriculum offers many opportunities for students to discover food from around the world and we have a particular focus on sustainability with students developing their awareness and understanding of how they affect this in their local community. Throughout the curriculum, career pathways are promoted to raise awareness and aspirations, for example the different types of chefs and job roles in the hospitality industry. Future opportunities are highlighted with potential career pathways in the industry to raise aspirations; for example, year 7 look at job roles in the industry.

pageCache.pageTitle: Information Technology - Subjects - Everest Community Academy
pageCache.text:
Information Technology
We aim to inspire confident, creative, and critical thinkers in technology, providing essential skills, ethical understanding, and an innovative mindset. Through hands-on projects and real-world applications, we shape future leaders and problem-solvers.
We are dedicated to enriching students' learning with a curriculum that sparks curiosity and promotes creative problem-solving. Through enrichment opportunities like coding clubs, students develop problem-solving, collaboration, and critical thinking skills in real-world scenarios.
We foster a positive classroom culture where students feel secure and enthusiastic about sharing their thoughts and ideas. This supportive atmosphere not only empowers them to express their creativity but also unlocks their full potential as confident problem-solvers and collaborators in the field of technology. By encouraging curiosity and collaboration, we prepare our students to thrive in a rapidly evolving in real world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Business Studies - Subjects - Everest Community Academy
pageCache.text:
Business Studies
Business is a fast growing subject at Everest. In the study of Business, students get the opportunity to begin their journey in to the adult world. The subject investigates human resources, marketing, finance and business planning. It provides students with an inspirational insight in to how a unique idea scribbled on a post-it note can turn in to a multi-million-pound business.
The GCSE course looks at the nature of business using business models, theories and techniques to support contemporary business issues the students will see in the media. The subject engages students as all topics are relevant to today’s society, they are able to apply their knowledge easily to their own day to day life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Health & Social Care - Subjects - Everest Community Academy
pageCache.text:
Health & Social Care
Health and Social Care explores the values of care, empathy and wellbeing at its heart. Students apply their learning to real-life scenarios through the three components. The course allows the students to develop their knowledge of human lifespan development, health and social care services and values and finally health and wellbeing. Emotional development is a crucial area of the Health and Social Care curriculum and is linked directly to physical and intellectual wellbeing. Students develop an empathetic approach to working with people and explore how others can be supported. Problem solving, teamwork and presentations allow for students to collaborate and build on skills which can push them out of their comfort zone. Students can see care workers demonstrating the skills, attributes and values either through videos or through care home visits and can demonstrate them themselves.
The Health and Social Care curriculum hopes to give students an insight to the services and values of the care industry and produce a more rounded individual who can understand other people better after looking at all the four developments over a person's lifespan.
Students apply their learning to real-life scenarios through the three components. The course allows the students to develop their knowledge of human lifespan development, health and social care services and values and finally health and wellbeing. It is 60% coursework based (which involves essay writing but also demonstrating the care values) and 40% exam based (which involves applying all their knowledge in a real-life scenario).
